pages.title: Getting Started
pages.summary: Spawn rules, starter tools, and your first objectives.

sections.title: Spawn Plaza
sections.contentMarkdown:
Spawn is a safe zone with repair stations, quest NPCs, and the map board.

Use /home to set a return point once you leave the plaza.

- Grab your starter kit from the supply chest.
- Pick a direction: north is tundra, south is forests.
- Check the daily bounty board for extra rewards.

sections.title: The Nether Gate
sections.contentMarkdown:
The Nether Gate activates once the Stone Warden is defeated.

Bring fire resistance and soul sand boots for safer travel.

sections.title: Behavior
sections.contentMarkdown:
The Abyssal Wyrm patrols flooded caverns between Y-20 and Y-40.

It retreats into water when below 40% health, summoning drownlings.

sections.title: Loot Table

- Wyrm Scale (x1-2)
- Abyssal Core (rare)
- Echo Pearl

sections.title: True Iron Fist
sections.contentMarkdown:
Three shards can be combined at the Obsidian Anvil to unlock the Rift ritual.

Completing the ritual reveals additional lore pages in the wiki.

sections.title: True Iron Fist's Journal
sections.contentMarkdown:
### True Iron Fist's Journal
"Damn it you killed me! Do you have any idea what you've done!? My task for centuries was to protect the inner sanctum. Every day for 900 years I pushed a button that has benefited you adventurers greatly. No wonder my master left human civilization. 

Humans take everything for granted. How did you get here anyways? Hm A mysterious voice guiding you you say? No.... it can't be. Listen to me traveler, No matter what he says, do not listen to the voice. He wants to get rid of the button. You see, the voice you've been talking to is that of a powerful necromancer named Rumpelstiltskin. 

Rumpel has one goal, to help monsters take over the universe. The button is what gives monsters their vulnerability to the sun. If he removes it this world will enter chaos! You must not listen to him!

pages.title: Mage
pages.summary: Staff-based spellcaster with reflect, burst spells, and control tools.

sections.title: Overview And Stat Focus
sections.contentMarkdown:
Stat focus: ARC, INT. Energy type: mana.

Mage scales heavily through casting throughput and range windows.

Key scaling notes:
- Passive mana return scales with INT (`int/10`)
- Neptune, Explosion Spell, and Energy Flux include INT/ARC formulas
- Chronoprohiberis cooldown and duration/range include ARC and INT
- Shared class scaling applies for VIT/INT/ARC/MIT baselines

sections.title: Abilities
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Mage Passive: Hoe/staff attacks restore mana and improve weapon output.
- Reflect: Chance to return damage when attacked with a staff.
- Neptune: Trident enhancement with lightning and multi-trident follow-up chances.
- Explosion Spell: Chance-based damage burst while attacking with a staff.
- Heal Spell: Extra regeneration when below a health threshold.
- Energy Flux: Right-click hoe beam attack with scaling line damage/range.
- Chronoprohiberis: Clock-triggered local time-stop with control effects.

pages.title: A Mysterious New Friend
pages.summary: A strange meeting with Crowley, a forgotten being bound in the void, that reveals the fractured legacy of Crash Cringle.

items.name: Totem of Undying
items.description: A rare item Crowley asks for while preparing to escape his magical restraints.

items.name: Gunpowder
items.description: Used as sulphur in Crowley's ritual to create the Sesro Shears.

items.name: [SF] Soulbound Rune
items.description: A slimefun soulbound rune used in the ritual to create the Sesro Shears.

items.name: Shears
items.description: Ordinary shears that are transformed through Crowley's ritual.

items.name: Sesro Shears
items.description: Magical shears created from sulphur, shears, and a Soulbound Rune. Used to cut Crowley free from his cuffs.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
You find **Crowley** bound somewhere deep and unpleasant, surprised that a living adventurer has managed to stumble into his prison. His first impression is hardly warm: he complains about the smell, mocks your appearance, and only then introduces himself as a forgotten, all-powerful being trapped in a body and restrained by magical cuffs.

Crowley claims that **Crash** is responsible for imprisoning him, and he quickly turns the conversation toward a bargain. If you help free him, he promises a reward. The task begins simply enough on paper: gather **sulphur**, a **Totem of Undying**, **shears**, and a **Soulbound Rune** so Crowley can craft a way out of his magical restraints.

sections.title: Freeing Crowley
sections.contentMarkdown:
Crowley cannot be freed by ordinary force. The cuffs on his hands radiate with enough power that even bending or breaking the metal directly is not an option. Instead, Crowley wants the materials for what he describes as a pair of “magic scissors.”

To continue, bring Crowley the full set of requested items: **64 Gunpowder**, **1 Totem of Undying**, **1 Soulbound Ancient Rune**, and **1 pair of Shears**. Once everything is gathered, return to Crowley so he can explain the ritual needed to create the **Sesro Shears** and cut him loose.

sections.title: After Crowley Is Freed
sections.contentMarkdown:
After you return with Crowley’s ingredients, he explains the ritual: make a pile of sulphur, bury the shears inside it, and drop the Soulbound Rune onto the pile. The mixture sizzles and creates a pair of **Sesro Shears**, which are then used to cut Crowley free from his cuffs.

Once freed, Crowley reveals that the Totem of Undying was not really for the shears at all. Instead, it leads into a much larger truth: the world is in danger. According to Crowley, **Crash Cringle** was once the physical embodiment of Matrix itself. When Crash was “killed” during a great war, reality could not simply stop existing, so Crash split into multiple forms. Each form represents a different part of reality, and each has plagued the world in its own way.

Crowley chooses you as the person who will help gather these forms back together and restore balance. He leaves to investigate which “realix” has the strongest foothold in the world, promising that you will be in touch — though he dodges the question of your promised reward.

sections.title: Quest Details
sections.contentMarkdown:
## Quest Details

- **Quest ID:** `0`
- **Quest Name:** **A Mysterious New Friend**
- **Starter NPC:** `citizens#30` — Crowley
- **Required Skill Level:** greater than `3`
- **Primary Objective:** Help free Crowley from his prison.
- **Objective Text:** *god these things are not comfortable*
- **Completion Reward:** Grants the player `matrix.quest.rescueCrowley`
- **Stage Reward:** `10` quest XP and `1000` skill XP after the opening conversation.

## Required Items

- **1x Totem of Undying**
- **64x Gunpowder** — referred to by Crowley as sulphur
- **1x Ancient Rune [Soulbound]**
- **1x Shears**

## Important Terms

- **Crowley:** A forgotten, powerful being trapped in a body and bound by magical cuffs.
- **Crash:** The being Crowley says trapped him.
- **Crash Cringle:** A mystical being described as the physical embodiment of Matrix.
- **Realix:** The term Crowley uses for the split forms/fragments of Crash Cringle.
- **Sesro Shears:** The magically created shears used to cut Crowley free.

sections.title: Lore Revealed
sections.contentMarkdown:
Crowley’s story reframes Matrix as a world still suffering from the aftermath of an ancient war. Crash Cringle was not merely powerful; he was tied directly to the structure of reality. His death caused Matrix to fracture into separate embodied forces, each one representing a different aspect of the world and each one causing damage in its own way.

The quest also leaves Crowley intentionally ambiguous. He presents himself as an ally and chooses the player over “some other able body,” but he also admits that, once free, he *could* have simply turned the player to ash and left. The result is a partnership built less on trust and more on mutual usefulness — Crowley needs someone active in the world, and the player needs answers about the larger danger facing Matrix.

pages.title: Find an Old Friend
pages.summary: Crowley sends you to find Flames, a lost soul who knows more about the Realixes and the strange fate awaiting the souls of Matrix.

items.name: Amber
items.description: A hardened golden gem acquired from resin. Flames asks for Amber before helping you further on your journey.

stats.value: A rare material in this world

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
Crowley reaches out through a projection, still trapped where you first found him even after being freed from his cuffs. He explains that the same spell binding him to his body also fixed him to that place, but he has still been able to explore through the spirit world and gather information.

This quest expands the mystery of the **Realixes**. Crowley believes there are **six** of them, but only two are currently clear enough to track: **The Corruption** and **The Lost**. Corruption appears to be spreading through magic, twisting both people and the world itself. The Lost is harder to understand, so Crowley sends you to find an old friend named **Flames**, a soul left wandering after the war.

sections.title: Seeking Flames
sections.contentMarkdown:
Crowley cannot explain The Lost on his own, so he points you toward **Flames**, a lost soul who has been roaming the world without a true destination. Flames may not appear like an ordinary person, and Crowley warns that you will likely see him as he sees himself — or at least as he wants to be seen.

Your next step is to locate Flames near spawn and ask him what he knows about the Realixes. The conversation quickly reveals that The Lost has dominion over souls, and that lost souls are not just spirits wandering by chance. They are connected to a larger imbalance in the world.

sections.title: What Flames Reveals
sections.contentMarkdown:
After speaking with Flames, the nature of **The Lost Realix** becomes clearer. The Lost has dominion over souls and direct control over lost souls like Flames. Flames explains that everyone becomes a lost soul eventually, but he also makes it clear that this is not how the world is supposed to work. Souls being "lost" after death is a symptom of the Realix's influence.

Flames also reveals that a Realix cannot truly be destroyed because it is woven into reality itself. What can be defeated is the Realix's living or physical manifestation. However, removing that manifestation creates a vacancy; something must take its place. The answer lies in special **Totems**, which can store living Realixes and lock them away from disturbing the natural balance of the world.

To begin tracking The Lost, Flames asks for **Amber**, a rare material formed from resin. Once you bring enough Amber, Flames tells you that The Lost does not usually interact with the living world. If you want to reach him, you will need to get his attention by collecting more souls and following a clue written in an unreadable, enchanting-table-like script.

sections.title: Quest Details
sections.contentMarkdown:
## Quest Details

- **Quest Name:** **Find an Old Friend**
- **Main Characters:** **Crowley** and **Flames**
- **Primary Objective:** Speak with Flames and learn more about The Lost Realix.
- **Secondary Objective:** Bring Flames enough **Amber** so he can help point you toward The Lost.
- **Required Item:** **30x Amber**
- **Follow-up:** This quest leads directly into the next part of the main Realix storyline.

## Important Concepts

- **Spirit World:** A realm Crowley claims to have explored while still bound to his prison.
- **Realixes:** Six powerful aspects of reality born from the fractured state of Matrix.
- **The Corruption:** A Realix associated with magic, corruption, and planted seeds of corruption throughout the world.
- **The Lost:** A Realix with dominion over souls and control over lost souls.
- **Totems:** Special vessels capable of storing living Realixes and preventing them from manipulating the world's natural balance.
- **Amber:** A rare resin-born material Flames requests before guiding you further.

sections.title: Lore Revealed
sections.contentMarkdown:
Crowley confirms that there are believed to be **six Realixes** in the world. Each Realix governs part of reality, but that does not necessarily mean every part of their domain is evil by itself. Magic, for example, belongs to Corruption's domain, but Crowley distinguishes between magic existing as part of the world and Corruption actively using it to twist people and plant seeds of corruption.

Flames deepens the lore around death and souls. The world has normalized lost souls, but Flames says this is not natural. The Lost Realix has made the loss of souls upon death feel ordinary, when in truth it is a distortion of the world's intended balance.

The quest also introduces the key method for dealing with Realixes: they are not simply killed. Their physical manifestations can be defeated, but their place in reality must be contained or replaced. The special Totems are the first clear path toward capturing them without letting reality collapse further out of balance.

pages.title: Explore the Ruins
pages.summary: After learning about The Lost, you gather souls, decode Flames' clue, and discover a hidden ruin containing two stranded adventurers and a broken portal.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
After speaking with **Flames**, you are left with two strange instructions: collect souls, and follow a location spoken in a language you cannot understand. The first part is grim but direct. If **The Lost** has dominion over souls, then gathering different kinds of souls may be enough to draw his attention or prepare you for whatever comes next.

The clue itself remains unreadable until you return to **Crowley**. When you repeat Flames' distorted words, Crowley recognizes the language immediately as "enchanting table" and realizes Flames was giving coordinates. The path now points toward the **Lost Ruins**, a remote and dangerous place that may hold the next sign of The Lost Realix.

sections.title: Gathering Souls
sections.contentMarkdown: Before following Flames' clue, you decide to gather a variety of different souls to cover your bases. You decide to gather souls from several sources: **players**, **drowned**, **phantoms**, **chickens**, **glow squids**, and **zombies**. Once enough souls have been gathered, return to Crowley and explain what Flames told you.

sections.title: The Lost Ruins
sections.contentMarkdown:
Crowley translates Flames' clue into a location and sends you to investigate the **Lost Ruins**. The ruins are located far from spawn, around **x=10,005, y=80, z=811**.

The journey is not only about reaching the ruins, but also about discovering what still remains there. Flames implied that this place may bring you closer to The Lost, but what you find is stranger than a simple shrine or dungeon.

sections.title: What Was Found in the Ruins
sections.contentMarkdown:
Inside the ruins, you find two stranded adventurers: **BatTiger** and **Mjfaithyuan**. They are thrilled to see you, but they have no intention of leaving. According to them, they originally came to the ruins looking for treasure, only to be chased away and forced into hiding.

Their discovery turns out to be far more important than diamonds. The real treasure of the ruins was a **secret portal** leading to a desolate town. On the other side, they encountered a disturbing figure calling himself **Rogue Crash**. Unfortunately, the portal was broken after they found it — but not destroyed in the normal sense. Mjfaithyuan explains that when he broke it, the portal somehow became lodged inside him.

The portal still exists, but it can only be accessed through Mjfaithyuan. Speak to him to gain entry into the valley.

sections.title: Quest Details
sections.contentMarkdown:
## Quest Details

- **Quest Name:** **Explore the Ruins**
- **Main Characters:** **Crowley**, **BatTiger**, and **Mjfaithyuan**
- **Primary Objective:** Gather souls, decode Flames' clue, and investigate the Lost Ruins.
- **Location:** **Lost Ruins**, around **x=10,005, y=80, z=811**
- **Follow-up:** Speak with **Mjfaithyuan** to access the strange portal hidden within him.

## Soul-Gathering Objectives

- **10x Player souls**
- **20x Drowned souls**
- **10x Phantom souls**
- **10x Chicken souls**
- **5x Glow Squid souls**
- **15x Zombie souls**

## Important Discoveries

- Flames' unreadable clue was written or spoken in enchanting table script.
- The Lost Ruins contain a hidden portal.
- The portal leads to a desolate town.
- A figure named **Rogue Crash** exists beyond the portal.
- The portal was broken, but somehow became trapped inside **Mjfaithyuan**.

sections.title: Lore Revealed
sections.contentMarkdown: This is the introduction to the "Lost Valley"

pages.title: Lost Valley
pages.summary: The trail leads deeper into uncharted territory.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"Readyyyyy? :D Let's GOOOOOOO"*

The mood is high as your group pushes into the Lost Valley. What you find there sends things in a new direction entirely.

pages.title: The Lost Valley
pages.summary: Someone — or something — is waiting in the valley, and they are not happy to see you.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"What part of 'Leave now' did you not understand?"*
> *"You know who I am."*

Not everyone here is a stranger. Press forward and uncover what this valley is hiding.

pages.title: The Order
pages.summary: You encounter the Order — a faction long cut off from the rest of the world.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"Well look who showed up."*
> *"Ignore him — he's kind of a buzzkill. His son's lost all hope."*

The Order has been waiting. Their situation is grim, but they may be the allies you need.

pages.title: The First Sacred Rite
pages.summary: Ancient trials overseen by a keeper of old knowledge. The first rite begins here.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"Ah, so you wish to complete the first sacred rite? Please, come closer — let me speaketh you the knowledge."*

Listen carefully. The keeper does not repeat herself.

pages.title: The Second Sacred Rite
pages.summary: The trials grow more complex. Your progress is acknowledged, but greater challenges await.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"You are well on your way. The next trials may prove to be more challenging in different ways."*

> *"Well, the first trial was fairly simple. It's what I do best."*

Confidence carries you into the second rite — whether or not it should.

pages.title: The Third Sacred Rite
pages.summary: The final rite demands everything. What comes after is not what you expected.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"I am proud of you. You have yet to take a bite from the forbidden fruit."*

> *"...yet?"*

The keeper's words carry a warning. Completing the third rite opens a door you cannot close.

pages.title: The Dark Path
pages.summary: The consequences of the sacred rites become real. This is where choices matter most.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
What the keeper called the "forbidden fruit" is no longer a metaphor.

The dark path is not for everyone — but you're already on it.

pages.title: Desperation
pages.summary: Someone is running out of time and you may be their last hope.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"Hm, what do you want? Didn't I already tell you I'm busy?"*
> *"Isn't everyone on the planet dying, just at a different rate?"*

> *"Please — you have to help me. I think I'm dying."*

Not everyone will take you seriously. Find someone who will.

pages.title: Moneybaggs
pages.summary: A rough journey leaves you worse for wear. Something broke — but what?

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"So... how was your journey? By the looks of you, not well."*

> *"All I know is when I went down there and talked to him he broke."*

The consequences of what happened are beginning to surface.

pages.title: Prison Break
pages.summary: An unlikely proposition from a fellow prisoner — a plan to escape.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"Psst, hey kid. Listen — I've got a way to bust us both out of this joint."*

> *"Uhh, what if I'd like to serve my time like a good citizen?"*

A classic jailbreak scenario. Cooperate — or don't.

pages.title: Darkness in its Prime
pages.summary: Facing forces that will stop at nothing, you must weigh the cost of your convictions.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"What's it gonna be, kid? Are you really going to risk your quest to save the..."*

> *"Okay — but torturing for answers isn't right either."*

The stakes are rising, and so are the moral choices.

pages.title: New Dawn
pages.summary: Rescued and regrouping aboard a strange ship, the path ahead starts to take shape.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"Relax — you're safe now. You're on our ship. We rescued you and your friends from that..."*

> *"What the—"*

A new chapter begins from an unexpected vantage point.

pages.title: Brothers?
pages.summary: A guild with deep roots — and a nagging sense that you have been here before.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"You've actually been here many times. This is your Adventurers Guild!"*

> *"Wow — this place is incredible."*

The guild feels familiar in ways you can't quite explain. Something happened here, and the answers are close.

pages.title: The Sewers
pages.summary: Pam and Prime have a monster problem beneath the city. Time to investigate.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"Good afternoon. Yes — Prime mentioned you have a problem with monsters?"*

A straightforward task on the surface. Clear out whatever is lurking in the sewers — or try to.

pages.title: Gathering
pages.summary: Regrouping and refocusing — the guild turns its attention back to the bigger picture.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"Indeed. I think it's high time we get back on target."*

> *"Well, the future certainly is interesting."*

With a clearer mission in mind, the guild readies itself for what comes next.

pages.title: Dream?
pages.summary: A glimpse of something that should not exist — a new dimension, and Crowley wants answers.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"Crowley... I don't know how to explain what I just witnessed."*
> *"A new dimension you say? Do you think you might've discovered one of the Realix's domains?"*

What you experienced defies explanation. Crowley is intrigued — and alarmed.

pages.title: Just a Dream
pages.summary: Crowley is furious and skeptical. But what you saw was real.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"This is bloody ridiculous. What kind of fool do you take me for?"*
> *"Have you tried just getting a permit? How hard is it?"*

Crowley's anger may be covering for something else. The events you witnessed are more real than anyone wants to admit.

pages.summary: The end of a long road — but Barlion stands in the way.

sections.title: Overview
sections.contentMarkdown:
> *"Crowley, we're almost done. Long story short — I have to become..."*

The finish line is in sight, but the path is never straightforward.

pages.title: Evil Containment Field
pages.summary: The Evil Containment Field is an ancient sealing technique invented by the heretics to keep corrupted magic under control in key areas.

sections.title: History
sections.contentMarkdown:
The Evil Containment Field is a powerful ancient sealing technique created by the heretics long ago in an effort to protect their people from unholy magic.

Most records describe it as both a defensive ritual and a purification tool. It was commonly built around watch posts, reliquaries, and temporary war camps where corruption's influence was strongest.

The original doctrine was simple: if corruption cannot be destroyed, it can be contained

Older heretic notes mention that these fields were used to prevent the watchful eye of the spectres. By nullifying their magic they became nothing more than beefier endermen. In some cases, they were also used as trial circles for suspected cultists and possessed warriors.

Even now, the technique remains prevelant as no one can escape it's power...not even the creators of this land. Anyone standing inside the field will be nullified, including the one who built it.

sections.title: Mechanics
sections.contentMarkdown:
### How to create one

Build a square with **4 Respawn Anchors** at the corners.

- The square must be between **8x8 and 11x11**.
- All anchors must be on the same Y level.
- The field only functions while at least one total charge exists across the 4 anchors.

### What it does

If a player is inside the active field range:

- Spell casts are cancelled.
- Teleports are cancelled and the player is pulled back.
- Commands are blocked.
- If lethal damage would kill the player, the field can nullify that death event.

Each successful nullification consumes charge from the anchors.

### Practical notes

- Keep spare glowstone ready. A drained field is just a square.
- Larger squares give better movement room but are easier to breach physically.
- Smaller squares are better for holding a single target or controlling choke points.
- If anchors are broken or moved, field integrity can fail immediately.

### Recommended setup

For a reliable containment site:

1. Mark your corner coordinates first.
2. Place all 4 anchors at matching height.
3. Charge all anchors before engaging the target.
4. Keep one runner outside with extra glowstone.

sections.title: Potential Applications
sections.contentMarkdown:
Legends say the heretics would form a square, then stack that square upward toward the sky to ensure purity at all angles.

According to these accounts, this was done to stop the Spectres of Chaos from observing them through distant sight or magical surveillance.

If the legends are true, the Evil Containment Field was used for more than local control. It was used to create blind zones where chaos entities could not cast, track, or watch.

Possible modern uses:

- Sealing a ritual site before a major boss encounter.
- Blocking teleport escapes during PvP
- Creating protected zones for farms
- Building layered perimeter rings around high-value structures.

Some scholars argue the stacked-field method may be the reason certain ruined towers still show strange anti-magic behavior today.
